speaker: richard_field
text: You want a chronicle. You shall hear me first, where the shop can hear it. Plays are a waste. A waste with a crowd in it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have heard you. I still want the second volume.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Mind your sleeve, Master Shakespeare. The quire under your elbow is still wet. I will move the quire. I am not moving his lecture.

speaker: richard_field
text: You may have the book when the shop has had the sentence. A playhouse takes a crowd and gives it back louder. A book stays where I put it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not asking you to love a playhouse. I am asking for the reign. The book can wait at the top of the stair while you finish.

speaker: richard_field
text: You will not read it on this floor. The floor is for the telling-off. Upstairs is for the book.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Upstairs is ready when your sleeve is safe. One wet cuff is enough ink for a visit.

speaker: richard_field
text: You have printed nothing of your own that a crowd can shout. Venus sits quiet. Lucrece sits quiet. That is a trade. A play is a noise with a receipt.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The noise keeps a company. I did not come to defend it on your shop floor. You have said waste. The shop has had it.

speaker: richard_field
text: Plays are a waste, and a waste with a crowd in it. There. Said to you, and said where the prentices can hear. I will not say it a third time.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twice is the shop's portion. I will not answer it down here.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Then both of you may go up. I am taking a candle. I am not taking the lecture with it.

speaker: richard_field
text: You are not to buy a poem on the way, either. If Daniel is still two shillings, he can stay two shillings. He is not my shelf.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not buying him. Two shillings was too dear when I stood over him, and it is still too dear. I came for your book.

speaker: richard_field
text: My book is Holinshed. The second volume. You will feel what it weighs on the stair, not down here, where a speech about a crowd is easy.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: If it is heavy, one of you carries it and the other opens the door. My arms are for the quires.

speaker: richard_field
text: You have had the lecture. Come up. And you will say nothing more in defence of a crowd until your shoes are off my floor.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nothing more on the floor. The crowd can wait for a yard that is not this one.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: The stair is clear. Go, before the wet quire finds the other sleeve.

speaker: richard_field
text: You will bring it home again. I am not giving it. I am lending it, which is a different verb, and you will hear that verb upstairs.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know the difference. I have not got it in my hands yet, and I am already not the owner.

speaker: richard_field
text: You know it because the shop has heard me. Upstairs I will say it otherwise.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Otherwise can wait for the stair. The candle is lit. I am not standing in a doorway to be an audience.

speaker: richard_field
text: One volume. The second. You are not taking the first off the shelf to keep it company.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The second. No Daniel. No speech down here in defence of the noise. After you.
